summary: A Stack Overflow question asks why 'docker stack deploy' fails with 'No such image: myuser/myrepo:mytag' for a private Docker Hub image, while 'docker-compose up' works. The accepted answer (by the asker, ice_chrysler) explains that the stack was deployed to a swarm worker node lacking registry credentials, fixed by using --with-registry-auth or deploying to a node holding the image. The page also includes several other answers listing additional causes: insecure registry settings not applied on all nodes, expired CI registry tokens, full disk space on a node, corporate VPN/proxy issues, and a private registry run as a container instead of a service.
one_line: Stack Overflow thread on why docker stack deploy reports 'No such image' for a private registry image, with causes and fixes from several answers.
key_facts: The question asks why 'docker stack deploy -c docker-compose.yml myapp' fails with "No such image: myuser/myrepo:mytag" while 'docker-compose up' works.
The question was asked on Nov 24, 2017 and was viewed about 32k times.
The asker had successfully run 'docker pull myuser/myrepo:mytag' before deploying and tried 'docker system prune' without success.
The accepted answer states the swarm stack was deployed to a worker node rather than the manager node the asker expected.
The accepted answer says the worker had no credentials to pull the image from the private repository.
The accepted answer suggests passing the flag --with-registry-auth to push repository credentials to the worker node.
A 2020 answer notes that deploying to an insecure registry fails if daemon.json is not edited on the server pulling the image.
A 2023 answer reports that a GitLab registry token valid for deploying to master was not valid for workers because the GitLab job had ended.
A 2023 answer reports that a swarm node running out of disk space produced the same error as an opaque message.
A 2022 answer reports that creating a service without a compose file using the same image URL worked, after which compose-file deployments also worked.
A 2023 answer says a private registry must be run as a SERVICE rather than just a container on the swarm manager node.
Konrad's comment describes intermittent failures using --prune, --with-registry-auth and --resolve-image=always with a private registry.
